allies.rationale_text: Scaffolding helps analogies-and-metaphors work by giving a staged bridge from what the audience already knows to what it needs to learn next.
allies.source_quote: Analogies and metaphors are strongest when people do not yet have a usable mental bucket for the new concept but do have adjacent experience that can carry the explanation.
allies.affinity_rationale: Described as the structural mechanism — 'Analogies provide the pre-existing mental model (the scaffold) off which new material can be piggybacked and built upon incrementally' — direct enabling mechanism for how analogies support learning.
allies.activation_condition: When the audience does not yet have a usable mental model for the new concept but does have working knowledge in a structurally similar domain

antagonists.rationale_text: Representativeness-heuristic undermines analogies-and-metaphors by driving analogy selection toward superficial surface similarity rather than deep structural correspondence, producing comparisons that feel right but mislead.
antagonists.source_quote: The primary challenge is either failing to see the conceptual similarity between domains or developing analogies based on superficial features, leading to poor quality ideas.
antagonists.affinity_rationale: Described as 'the primary challenge' — analogies built on surface-level similarity rather than verified structural similarity between domains produce misleading transfers.
antagonists.activation_condition: When analogies are being selected based on surface resemblance rather than verified structural similarity between the source and target domains

antagonists.rationale_text: Einstellung-effect undermines analogies-and-metaphors by locking onto the first familiar comparison so firmly that the thinker never tests whether a different analogy would map the target domain more accurately.
antagonists.source_quote: This occurs when thinkers persist in using mental models that are unhelpful or misleading in a new context.
antagonists.affinity_rationale: Related persistence mechanism — 'thinkers persist in using mental models that are unhelpful or misleading in a new context' — about stickiness of old analogies rather than a direct attack on analogical reasoning itself.
antagonists.activation_condition: When familiar analogies from past experience persist in guiding thinking even though the new context requires a genuinely different framing

structured_tensions.tension_text: Analogies-and-metaphors conflicts with abstraction when vivid analogy transfer distorts the structural boundaries of the target domain.
structured_tensions.source_quote: analogies-and-metaphors vs abstraction: analogies-and-metaphors conflicts with abstraction (abstraction) when vivid analogy transfer distorts the structural boundaries of the target domain.

structured_tensions.tension_text: Analogies-and-metaphors conflicts with cognitive-load-theory when layered metaphors increase interpretation burden instead of reducing it.
structured_tensions.source_quote: analogies-and-metaphors vs cognitive-load-theory: analogies-and-metaphors conflicts with cognitive-load-theory (cognitive load theory) when layered metaphors increase interpretation burden instead of reducing it.
